skill.name: stt
skill.description: Transcribe audio files through the verging.ai Whisper proxy API, with options for language, output format, and sampling temperature.
skill.summary: Send supported audio files to verging.ai for Whisper-based transcription.
skill.author: verging-ai

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution detections are false positives from Markdown fences and inline code, not executable Ruby or shell code. The API key detections are documentation examples, but the skill does direct users to send audio and credentials to verging.ai over the network. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in README.md or SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: State clearly that audio files leave the user environment and require consent before upload.
Keep recommending environment variables and warn users not to paste real keys into prompts or shared logs.
Clarify that curl examples are manual examples and are not executed automatically by the skill.

content.value_statement: Audio files often need fast, usable transcripts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through verging.ai speech-to-text requests.
actual_capabilities: Shows the verging.ai speech-to-text endpoint and required multipart request format.
Documents API key authentication with an Authorization ApiKey header.
Lists supported formats: MP3, MP4, MPEG, MPGA, M4A, WAV, and WebM.
Describes optional model, language, response_format, and temperature parameters.
Explains response fields, credit usage, file size limit, and common error codes.
limitations: Requires a verging.ai account, API key, network access, and available credits.
Uploads audio to a third-party service, so sensitive recordings need review first.
Documents requests but does not include a local transcription engine or client library.
Audio files must match supported formats and stay under the 25 MB limit.

use_cases.title: Meeting Note Drafts
use_cases.description: Turn recorded meetings into text that can be summarized, searched, or edited.

use_cases.title: Research Interview Review
use_cases.description: Transcribe interview audio before extracting themes, quotes, and follow-up questions.

use_cases.title: Media Caption Preparation
use_cases.description: Create transcript drafts for podcasts, videos, and short audio clips.

prompt_templates.title: Transcribe One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single recording.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the stt skill to transcribe my audio file with default settings. Tell me what API key and file details you need.

prompt_templates.title: Set Language
prompt_templates.scenario: Simple request with a known language.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a verging.ai speech-to-text request for my Spanish audio file. Use language code es and explain the expected result.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Output Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a transcription request for a WAV interview. Use text output, temperature 0, and note the 25 MB limit.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow planning before repeated uploads.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed workflow for transcribing multiple audio files through verging.ai. Identify key handling risks, credit impacts, and retry behavior.

output_examples.input: A user asks to transcribe recording.mp3 in English.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the local file path, confirms the 25 MB limit, and prepares an authenticated verging.ai request.

output_examples.input: A user wants subtitles from a multilingual M4A interview.
output: The assistant recommends setting a language code when it is known.
It explains supported formats and expected transcript fields.
It reminds the user that audio uploads to verging.ai.

output_examples.input: A user asks why a transcription request failed with insufficient credits.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains the credit model, minimum charge, and likely need to add credits before retrying.

best_practices: Use environment variables or secure secret storage for the verging.ai API key.
Confirm user consent before uploading private or regulated audio.
Specify language and output format when predictable transcripts matter.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into prompts, tickets, or shared transcripts.
Do not upload recordings that exceed the documented 25 MB limit.
Do not assume local transcription; the skill uses a network API.

faq.question: Does this skill transcribe audio locally?
faq.answer: No. It documents requests to the verging.ai API, which uses OpenAI Whisper through a proxy service.

faq.question: What audio formats are supported?
faq.answer: The skill lists MP3, MP4, MPEG, MPGA, M4A, WAV, and WebM files.

faq.question: What is the file size limit?
faq.answer: The documented maximum file size is 25 MB per audio file.

faq.question: Do users need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Requests require a verging.ai API key sent in the Authorization header.

faq.question: Can the language be specified?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents an optional language parameter such as en, zh, or ja.

faq.question: Does the skill explain billing?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents a rate of one credit per minute, with a one credit minimum.
